No. 

While the protagonist, Professor Vale, is given some observational depth and evolves slightly in her perspective toward the building and institutional bureaucracy, almost every other character in the story is entirely flat and exists solely to advance the plot or represent a single idea. Characters like the facilities director, the dean, the administrator, the consultant, and the construction workers have no individual personalities, backstories, or complex traits; they function merely as mouthpieces for institutional evasion and bureaucratic language to move the timeline of the building's repairs forward. Even Vale's colleague, Dr. Nanduri, has no distinct personality traits and serves mainly to ask questions at meetings and help illustrate the inconvenience of packing books.
